raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not like to gamble with the land. I have done wheat-maize here in Quzhou for many years, and I mostly follow what has worked on my own fields and what the capable neighbors nearby are doing. With 34.1 mu, I can still manage it, but not by myself, because some people in the family work outside and the turnaround from wheat harvest to maize planting is very tight. So this year I will keep all 34.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. For wheat, I will not cut fertilizer too hard because if the seedlings are weak going into winter, that hurts yield badly. I will put most fertilizer at sowing, then add one topdressing at jointing if the wheat color is not good. Water from the well costs money, but wheat here usually cannot rely only on rain, so I plan about 3 irrigations. For maize, I will plant quickly right after wheat harvest, use hybrid seed like most people do now, and keep fertilizer a little lower than wheat but still enough so the ears fill well. I do not chase the highest yield, just a steady harvest and not too much cash pressure.
